insecureContext.title: Insecure context
insecureContext.message: This page is served over plain HTTP. Browsers do not expose window.crypto.subtle in this context, which blocks all client-side cryptography (RSA generation, AES encryption, passphrase derivation).
insecureContext.why: Harpocrate runs all crypto in the browser (E2E zero-knowledge). Without a secure context, the vault simply cannot work — this is a Web standard restriction, not an app bug.
insecureContext.cert_warning: The certificate is self-signed in dev — your browser will show a warning. Accept it once ("Advanced → Continue").

hero.subtitle: A secrets manager where even the server operator cannot read your data. Cryptography runs entirely in your browser — the server stores only encrypted blobs.

zeroKnowledge.name: Zero Knowledge
zeroKnowledge.desc: Encryption happens in your browser via WebCrypto API and Argon2id. The server stores only ciphertext — your secrets are mathematically inaccessible to us.

devFirst.name: Developer First
devFirst.desc: Native CLI, Python SDK, and REST API with bearer tokens. Pull secrets directly into CI pipelines without storing credentials in environment files.

audit.name: Audit Everything
audit.desc: Immutable audit log streams every read, write, grant, and revocation to Loki. Know exactly who accessed what, from which IP, at what time.

s1.title: Generate your keypair
s1.desc: On first login, a 4096-bit RSA keypair is generated entirely in your browser. Your private key is encrypted with your passphrase via Argon2id — it never leaves your device in cleartext.

s2.title: Encrypt secrets locally
s2.desc: Each wallet holds a symmetric AES-256 key, itself encrypted with your public key. Secret values are encrypted client-side before upload. The server receives only opaque blobs.

s3.title: Share with precision
s3.desc: Grant colleagues access using a five-bit permission bitmap: READ, WRITE, ADD, REMOVE, INIT. Their public key encrypts the wallet key — access is cryptographically scoped.

privacy.label: Privacy & responsibility
privacy.title: Personal data & service limits
privacy.body: Harpocrate stores in plaintext only your e-mail address and display name — strictly the minimum needed to identify you inside your vault. All your secrets are encrypted client-side and remain unreadable to the server operator. Because the service is zero-knowledge, losing your passphrase or recovery phrase means the permanent and irreversible loss of your secrets: we cannot recover them for you.

footer.tagline: The god of silence keeps your secrets.

rgpd.label: Privacy policy
rgpd.title: Personal data & GDPR
rgpd.subtitle: Disclosure compliant with Articles 13 and 14 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

sections.title: 1. Data controller
sections.body: Harpocrate is self-hosted software. The data controller is the administrator (natural or legal person) who operates the instance you are registered on. To exercise your rights, contact that administrator directly; their contact information should be displayed at the root of the instance or in its legal notice.

sections.title: 2. Personal data collected
sections.body: The service collects a strict minimum of identifying data, stored in plaintext in the database:
bullets: E-mail address — used as a unique identifier and notification channel.
Display name — shown in the interface and in the audit log.
User identifier (UUID) generated automatically.
Technical timestamps: creation date, last vault unlock, quarantine.

sections.title: 3. Technical data tied to usage
sections.body: For security and traceability reasons, certain technical data is recorded in the audit log:
bullets: Connecting IP address (retention aligned with the configured log retention).
Identifiers of vaults and secrets accessed, without their content.
Type of action performed (read, write, share, revoke) and its timestamp.

sections.title: 4. What the server never sees
sections.body: Harpocrate is built on the zero-knowledge principle. The following items never leave your browser in plaintext and are never stored in plaintext on the server:
bullets: Your passphrase and recovery phrase.
Your RSA private key (encrypted locally before any transfer).
The content of the secrets themselves (values, passwords, API keys).

sections.title: 5. Purposes of processing
sections.body: Your data is processed exclusively to: (a) authenticate you on the instance, (b) let you decrypt your own vaults, (c) trace accesses in the audit log to detect potential misuse, and (d) notify you of important events (reset, sharing, quarantine).

sections.title: 6. Legal basis
sections.body: Processing is based on the performance of the service contract between you and the administrator of the instance (Article 6.1.b GDPR). Audit logging is based on the legitimate interest of the controller in securing the service (Article 6.1.f).

sections.title: 7. Retention period
sections.body: Identification data is kept as long as your account is active. The audit log is kept according to the Loki retention policy configured by the administrator (7 days by default). When your account is deleted, your identifying data is erased immediately; historical audit entries may persist until the normal retention expires.

sections.title: 8. Recipients & processors
sections.body: No data is transmitted to a commercial third party. Harpocrate contains no telemetry or external analytics. The only possible external dependencies are configured by the administrator: identity provider (Keycloak), remote backup storage (S3, SFTP, etc.), and log collector (Loki/Grafana). Each of these dependencies has its own policy, for which the administrator is responsible.

sections.title: 9. Your rights
sections.body: Pursuant to Articles 15 to 22 of the GDPR, you have the following rights:
bullets: Right of access — obtain a copy of your identifying data.
Right to rectification — correct your e-mail or display name.
Right to erasure — request the deletion of your account.
Right to portability — export your vaults in encrypted form.
Right to object — refuse certain processing purposes.
Right to lodge a complaint with the supervisory authority (CNIL in France, www.cnil.fr).

sections.title: 10. Security
sections.body: Communications are encrypted in transit (TLS). Secrets are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using a key derived from your passphrase via Argon2id, and the vault symmetric key is itself encrypted with your RSA-4096 public key. No secret is ever accessible in plaintext by the server operator.

sections.title: 1. Purpose
sections.body: These Terms of Service ("Terms") govern the use of the Harpocrate service, a zero-knowledge secrets manager, by any person holding an account on the relevant instance. They constitute a contract between you and the administrator of the instance.

sections.title: 2. Description of the service
sections.body: Harpocrate lets you store, organise and share secrets (passwords, API keys, tokens, certificates) encrypted end-to-end. Encryption and decryption are performed entirely in your browser; the server only receives and stores encrypted blobs. The operator has no technical means of accessing the content of your secrets.

sections.title: 3. Account & registration
sections.body: To use the service, you must create an account tied to a valid e-mail address and choose a passphrase meeting the minimum requirements shown at first login. You are solely responsible for keeping your credentials confidential. Any action taken from your account is presumed to come from you.

sections.title: 4. Loss of passphrase — critical notice
sections.body: Harpocrate is built on the zero-knowledge principle. This means that nobody, including the administrator of the instance, can recover your secrets if you lose both your passphrase and your recovery phrase. Without them, your secrets are mathematically and irreversibly inaccessible. Accordingly:
bullets: You acknowledge having understood this characteristic and accept it without reservation.
You undertake to keep your passphrase and recovery phrase in a safe place.
The service operator cannot in any way be held liable for the loss of your secrets resulting from forgetting, disclosing or destroying your secret credentials.
No recourse, financial or otherwise, is available to the user in this situation.

Attempting to compromise the security of the service or of other users' data.
